Subject: Re: Mid-contract capacity increase — need pricing options

Hi Alex — thanks for the heads up and the files. Maya — welcome.

High level we have three pragmatic paths we typically offer for mid-contract uplifts:

1) Commitment top-up (co-term): add the incremental units to the existing contract period and apply a stepped discount based on the uplift band. This keeps billing on your current renewal cadence and proration is applied for the remainder of the term.

2) Annualize new capacity: convert the uplift into a new 12-month commitment starting on the uplift date. This gets a larger discount since it extends the commitment window but requires an annual invoice cadence.

3) Temporary burst + credit: short-term burst capacity with usage credits applied to the next invoice while you lock in forecasts. This is useful for urgent spikes but is not intended for sustained 50% growth.

Ben — can you propose numbers for Orchard (ballpark % discounts per path and an example month-by-month invoice walkthrough)? Lauren, FYI in case CS needs to coordinate onboarding capacity.

I can also prepare a one-pager that compares the three options (cost delta, SLA impacts, and how KV-cache warmup would be handled operationally).

Best,
Soojin Lee
Director, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

On Thu, Jun 2, 2027 at 10:04 AM Soojin Lee wrote:
> Ben — can you propose numbers for Orchard (ballpark % discounts per path and an example month-by-month invoice walkthrough)?

Alex / team — attaching a quick pricing playbook with two structured proposals:

A) Co-term top-up (recommended for predictable growth)
 - Uplift: +50% committed units for remainder of term (prorated)
 - Discount: stepped 8% on the uplift amount if top-up confirmed within 10 business days; 5% if within 30 days
 - One-time onboarding credit: $8k if we run a Redwood-led performance tuning sprint (applies to first invoice)
 - Billing: prorated immediate charge + remainder billed on regular renewal cadence

B) Annualize uplift (recommended for multiyear commitment)
 - Uplift converted to a 12-month add-on starting on July 1
 - Discount: 12% on the new 12-month volume
 - Payment terms: net 30 on the annualized add-on or net 45 with purchase order

C) Short-term burst (interim)
 - Burst pool for 60 days with usage credits applied post-billing; fee to enable: $2k
 - Not eligible for volume discount until converted to a top-up

The playbook XLSX has a worked example and a token-level cost/latency sensitivity chart to help you pick.

Attachments: redwood_pricing_playbook_Q2.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

If Orchard prefers a hybrid (e.g., 25% top-up co-term + 25% burst), we can price that too — will need an expected run-rate to size the slabs.

Ben Carter
Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
